arguments.text: The narrative cites the fact that Barbara did not consult her usual charts during the assessment, which describes conduct rather than an explicit out-of-court assertion, potentially attacking the threshold requirement for hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires an out-of-court statement; mere conduct or circumstantial facts without intent to assert may not qualify as hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that Barbara didn't consult with her usual charts while assessing Elizabethg.

arguments.text: If the cited fact regarding the charts is construed as an assertion of Barbara's deviation from standard practice, it is offered to prove the truth of that matter (i.e., that the assessment was flawed), supporting a hearsay classification.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as an out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that Barbara didn't consult with her usual charts while assessing Elizabethg.

arguments.text: The narrative does not suggest the fact is offered for a non-hearsay purpose such as notice, effect on the listener, or impeachment, reinforcing the inference that it is offered for its truth.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) hearsay analysis hinges on the purpose for which the evidence is offered; absence of non-hearsay purpose supports truth-offering inference.
